text: dsh-auto-reconnect 是面向 DSH 网页客户端的自动重连插件，通过客户端注入连接服务，在页面重新可见、获得焦点或用户交互时唤醒连接控制器，并在进入断开状态后按次数预算重试。它也会在浏览器从缓存恢复页面时强制重连，并在控制台记录触发原因。用户可在浏览器 localStorage 调整重试间隔、次数上限和日志选项。适合希望减少网页客户端断线后手动恢复操作的 DSH 用户；不需要额外密钥或外部服务。

dsh-auto-reconnect restores the DSH web client connection after disconnects and page wake events. It retries within a configurable limit and responds to visibility, focus, and user input. Retry settings are stored in browser localStorage. No API key or external service is needed.
DSH 网页断开后能不能自己重连？
切回浏览器页面时自动恢复 DSH 连接。
Can my DSH web session reconnect automatically after it disconnects?
dsh-auto-reconnect 的功能「断线后自动重试」：连接状态进入 disconnected 时，插件按配置的延迟安排重连，并限制连续重试次数；恢复 connected 后重置计数。
dsh-auto-reconnect 的功能「页面唤醒连接」：页面变为可见、获得焦点、收到键盘或指针交互时尝试唤醒连接；从浏览器缓存恢复页面时则强制重连。

Auto-reconnect for the DeepSeek Harness (DSH) web client. The official connection controller has backoff reconnect built in, but it sleeps through two real-world scenarios — this plugin wakes it. Client-only, zero build, no official package touched.

dsh-auto-reconnect README · Install / Uninstall：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:tqcq/dsh-auto-reconnect
```

Then restart dsh-web — adding or removing plugins always needs a restart; a browser refresh alone is not enough.

Upgrade (re-running `add` won't move the resolved commit; `update` re-resolves):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web update dsh-auto-reconnect
```

Uninstall:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-auto-reconnect
```

dsh-auto-reconnect README · Two blind spots in the official controller (source-audited)：Audited against the actually-served `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-connection` 0.1.2-rc.1:
section: Two blind spots in the official controller (source-audited)

text:
dsh-auto-reconnect README · Two blind spots in the official controller (source-audited)：1. Terminal `disconnected` sleeps forever. Once the official 500ms→10s backoff tops out, the controller enters a terminal state and only wakes on the browser `online` event or a manual tap. Phone sleep/wake keeps `navigator.onLine === true` the whole time, so `online` never fires — every wake-up needs a manual tap.
2. Zombie `connected`. The official client has no visibilitychange / focus listener and no heartbeat. A silently dropped TCP leaves the WebSocket in OPEN while the state still reports `connected`.
section: Two blind spots in the official controller (source-audited)

text: dsh-auto-reconnect README · What this plugin does：Listens to `visibilitychange(→visible)`, `focus`, `pointerdown`, `keydown`, `pageshow(persisted)`, and subscribes to the connection state store:

dsh-auto-reconnect README · What this plugin does：- Event wakes: call `connection.reconnect()` only when state ≠ `connected` (resets backoff, retries immediately) — never interrupts a healthy connection.
- bfcache restore (`persisted`): sockets are dead by definition, reconnect unconditionally.
- Transition into terminal `disconnected`: delayed auto-retry (default 3s), budgeted to 20 consecutive attempts, reset on `connected`. Covers "page already visible and focused, no browser event will ever fire again" (2026-09-11 field report: a hard refresh after a host restart landed in terminal state, still needed a manual tap).
dsh-auto-reconnect README · What this plugin does：Every trigger logs with a `[dsh-auto-reconnect]` prefix (DevTools console forensics), throttled to 3s by default.

dsh-auto-reconnect README · Compatibility：- Field-verified on host `@deepseek-ai/dsh` 0.1.5-rc.2 (boot activation assertions all green).
- Client contract audited against `dsh-client-connection` 0.1.2-rc.1 source.
- Shape mismatch on `ctx.connection` → warn and stay idle, never breaks the page: graceful degradation on API drift.

dsh-auto-reconnect README · Limitations：The general form of zombie `connected` (background tab NAT-dropped, no OS sleep) cannot be detected client-side: the RPC unary channel is separate HTTP, so a successful probe does not prove the WebSocket is alive. The real fix is a host-side heartbeat + dead-connection sweep (prior art: the deprecated enterhalf/dsh-web-network-optimizer) — a separate plugin if ever needed.
